messages:
mike: Heads-up — we saw a sudden spike in queue_length on gpupartition-eu-west-2 around 00:12 UTC, admission started returning 429s.
anya: Yep noticed it in the dashboard, p95 latency for short seqs jumped from 80ms -> 300ms, and warm_pool_utilization hit ~98%.
leo: Any network flapping or node churn? I checked k8s events, only normal preemptions.
tori: cc @mike @leo I pulled the trace — it's mostly small chat completions, high qps burst from a single client region (APAC edge). Lots of new cold requests that missed prefix cache.
mike: Looks like warm-pool delta didn't keep up with the burst. Current config: warm_pool_target=0.15 per shard, prewarm_grace=30s. We have admission tokenbucket rate tied to provisioned_gpus.
leo: Proposal: temporarily increase warm_pool_target to 0.30 and lower prewarm_grace to 8s for the APAC pools, plus increase admission burst tokens by 20% to smooth short spikes.
anya: That will increase cost if kept long. Can we add a canary: ramp warm pool for 2h with autoscale cooldown 5min and check queue_length and denied_admissions metrics? If stable, rollback.
tori: Sounds good. Also we should enable short-request-prefill: true for this workload to populate KV caches quicker for chat completions.
ops-sre: Note about capacity: APAC region has a slower replenish time for GPUS (spot & reserved mix). If we overprewarm we risk starving other priority customers in the region.
mike: Agreed — limit scope to the dedicated-slo tier first. Add a routing policy to favor dedicated pools for this client rather than shared capacity.
infra-bot: deploy request queued: patch warmpool config -> warm_pool_target=0.30 in cluster apac-dedicated; change admission.burst=+20% for 2h; author=mike
leo: Small config snippet I propose:
```
warm_pool:
  target_fraction: 0.30
  prewarm_grace_seconds: 8
admission:
  burst_increase_percent: 20
  cooldown_seconds: 300
canary:
  duration_seconds: 7200
  success_criteria:
    - queue_length_p95 < 10
    - denied_admissions_rate < 0.5%
```
anya: Can we also add a quick alert if gpu_p95_latency exceeds 250ms for more than 3 consecutive windows? That should guard against regressions.
tori: I'll wire the alert and a Grafana panel. Also add a short term cost estimate: assuming 2h extra warm pool at +15% capacity -> ~ $420 extra for the window.
mike: Acceptable for a 2h canary. If it helps SLA we absorb.
ops-sre: After canary, we should adjust autoscaler smoothing: increase scale up step by 1 node per minute and add hysteresis on scale down (2m) to avoid oscillations.
leo: One more: add admission fallback route to cheaper quantized models when warm_pool_utilization > 95% so latency-sensitive requests get degraded gracefully instead of hard 429s.
anya: Nice. That gives graceful degradation instead of dropping. I'll coordinate with model-onboarding to mark compatible fallbacks.
infra-bot: deploy result: canary successfully applied to apac-dedicated (id: canary-1758881234), monitoring started.
mike: Monitoring shows queue_length_p95 down to 4 within 45s, denied_admissions down to 0.1%.
tori: :thumbsup: Looks stable so far, leaving canary for full 2h.
ops-sre: After this, let's do a post-mortem note with suggested long-term: smarter prewarm heuristics based on per-client burstiness and prefix-cache warming on first tokens.
anya: Agreed — will draft a short write-up and include the cost tradeoffs and our fallback policy recommendations.
mike: Thanks everyone. If anything regresses ping here or page ops-sre.
ops-sre: will do. Good job triaging. :wave:
